annotations.description:
Annotations on the Bare Metal Admin Cluster.
This field has the same restrictions as Kubernetes annotations.
The total size of all keys and values combined is limited to 256k.
Key can have 2 segments: prefix (optional) and name (required),
separated by a slash (/).
Prefix must be a DNS subdomain.
Name must be 63 characters or less, begin and end with alphanumerics,
with dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: annotations has no security impact on the service or data

bare_metal_version.description: The Anthos clusters on bare metal version for the admin cluster resource.
bare_metal_version.rationale: Bare metal version is a critical security parameter that determines the version of the bare metal admin cluster and can affect compliance with security requirements.

description.description: A human readable description of this Bare Metal Admin Cluster.
description.rationale: Description has no security impact on the service or data

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: The bare metal admin cluster name.
name.rationale: Display name has no security impact on the service or data

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: A resource identifier/pointer to the GCP project the cluster belongs to; project-level access is governed by IAM bindings elsewhere, not by this attribute.

cluster_operations.description: Specifies the Admin Cluster's observability infrastructure.

cluster_operations.enable_application_lo.description: Whether collection of application logs/metrics should be enabled (in addition to system logs/metrics).
cluster_operations.enable_application_lo.rationale: Toggles collection of application logs/metrics (in addition to system logs/metrics). This is security telemetry: without application-level logging, the cluster lacks the audit/visibility trail needed to detect or investigate anomalous workload behaviour. It should default to enabled rather than left off.

control_plane.api_server_args.description:
Customizes the default API server args. Only a subset of
customized flags are supported. Please refer to the API server
documentation below to know the exact format:
https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kube-apiserver/

control_plane.api_server_args.argument.description: The argument name as it appears on the API Server command line please make sure to remove the leading dashes.
control_plane.api_server_args.argument.rationale: Names one entry in an arbitrary key-value argument list; a generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain which flag names a customer chooses to pass without hardcoding an exhaustive allow/deny list of kube-apiserver flags, which is not a viable policy target here.

control_plane.api_server_args.value.description: The value of the arg as it will be passed to the API Server command line.
control_plane.api_server_args.value.rationale: The literal value paired with an api_server_args.argument entry carries no security meaning on its own - its effect depends entirely on which kube-apiserver flag (argument) it modifies, and argument itself was already assessed as carrying no security impact. The policy engine evaluates one attribute in isolation and cannot correlate value with its sibling argument name, so a check on value alone could not distinguish a sensitive flag (e.g. anonymous-auth) from a benign one (e.g. max-requests-inflight) and would be either meaningless or misleading.

control_plane.control_plane_node_pool_co.description: Configures the node pool running the control plane. If specified the corresponding NodePool will be created for the cluster's control plane. The NodePool will have the same name and namespace as the cluster.
The generic configuration for a node pool running the control plane.

The map of Kubernetes labels (key/value pairs) to be applied to
each node. These will added in addition to any default label(s)
that Kubernetes may apply to the node. In case of conflict in
label keys, the applied set may differ depending on the Kubernetes
version -- it's best to assume the behavior is undefined and
conflicts should be avoided. For more information, including usage
and the valid values, see:
  - http://kubernetes.io/v1.1/docs/user-guide/labels.html
An object containing a list of "key": value pairs.
For example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.
control_plane.control_plane_node_pool_co.rationale: Kubernetes labels are organisational metadata (grouping/selection); they carry no access-control or exposure implication.

control_plane.control_plane_node_pool_co.description: Specifies the nodes operating system (default: LINUX).
control_plane.control_plane_node_pool_co.rationale: Selects the node OS family for the control-plane node pool (default LINUX); this is a platform-compatibility choice, not an access or exposure control.

The default IPv4 address for SSH access and Kubernetes node.
Example: 192.168.0.1
control_plane.control_plane_node_pool_co.rationale: The IPv4 address of a specific control-plane node's host machine. Like load_balancer.vip_config.control_plane_vip and node_access_config.login_user on this resource, this is an environment-specific network value with no universal 'safe' setting - a generic policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding a customer's own IP addressing plan.

control_plane.control_plane_node_pool_co.description: The initial taints assigned to nodes of this node pool.
Specifies the nodes operating system (default: LINUX). Possible values: ["EFFECT_UNSPECIFIED", "PREFER_NO_SCHEDULE", "NO_EXECUTE"]
control_plane.control_plane_node_pool_co.rationale: Kubernetes scheduling taint effect; controls pod placement eligibility, not access or exposure.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.asn.description: BGP autonomous system number (ASN) of the cluster.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.asn.rationale: The BGP autonomous system number identifying the cluster's routing domain; an environment-specific network identifier, not an access or exposure control.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.address_pool.description:
a list of non-overlapping IP pools used
by load balancer typed services.
The addresses that are part of this pool.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.address_pool.rationale: The IP addresses/ranges assigned to the BGP address pool; environment-specific addressing, the same reasoning already applied to the CIDR block fields elsewhere on this resource.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.address_pool.description:
This avoids buggy consumer devices mistakenly
dropping IPv4 traffic for those special IP addresses.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.address_pool.rationale: A compatibility workaround for buggy consumer devices mishandling certain IPv4 addresses; has no security implication.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.address_pool.description: If true, prevent IP addresses from being automatically assigned.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.address_pool.rationale: Controls whether pool IPs are assigned automatically or manually; an operational choice with no access-control implication.
An identifier/name for the address pool; naming has no access-control implication.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.bgp_peer_con.description: BGP autonomous system number (ASN) of the cluster.
BGP autonomous system number (ASN) of the cluster.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.bgp_peer_con.rationale: The external BGP peer's autonomous system number; an environment-specific network identifier, not an access or exposure control.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.bgp_peer_con.description:
The IP address of the control plane node that
connects to the external peer.
load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.bgp_peer_con.rationale: IP addresses of the control-plane nodes that connect to the external BGP peer; environment-specific network values, the same reasoning already applied to node_ip on this resource.
The external BGP peer's IP address; an environment-specific network value with no universal 'safe' setting.

load_balancer.bgp_lb_config.load_balance.rationale: Selects the node OS family for the load-balancer node pool (default LINUX); a platform-compatibility choice, not an access or exposure control.

load_balancer.manual_lb_config.enabled.description: Whether manual load balancing is enabled.
load_balancer.manual_lb_config.enabled.rationale: Chooses manual load balancing over BGP/other modes; an infrastructure-topology choice with no inherently 'safe' state, the same reasoning already applied to load_balancer.vip_config and load_balancer.port_config on this resource.

load_balancer.port_config.control_plane_.description: The port that control plane hosted load balancers will listen on.
load_balancer.port_config.control_plane_.rationale: Sets the TCP port the control-plane load balancer listens on. A port number is an environment-specific value with no inherently 'secure' choice; constraining it would require hardcoding a port, which is overreaching and not a security archetype.

load_balancer.vip_config.description: Specified the Bare Metal Load Balancer Config

load_balancer.vip_config.control_plane_v.description: The VIP which you previously set aside for the Kubernetes API of this Bare Metal Admin Cluster.
load_balancer.vip_config.control_plane_v.rationale: A virtual IP address the team sets aside for the Kubernetes API. It is an environment-specific network value; a generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding an IP, so it is not a useful policy target.

maintenance_config.maintenance_address_c.description:
All IPv4 address from these ranges will be placed into maintenance mode.
Nodes in maintenance mode will be cordoned and drained. When both of these
are true, the "baremetal.cluster.gke.io/maintenance" annotation will be set
on the node resource.
maintenance_config.maintenance_address_c.rationale: The CIDR ranges that place matching nodes into maintenance mode are an operational networking assignment (which nodes get cordoned/drained for maintenance), not a security control.

network_config.advanced_networking.description: Enables the use of advanced Anthos networking features.
network_config.advanced_networking.rationale: Enables Bundled Load Balancing with BGP and the egress NAT gateway feature set (per Google's Distributed Cloud bare metal cluster-configuration reference) - a networking-architecture capability toggle, not an access-control or authentication setting. It does not gate Kubernetes NetworkPolicy enforcement: GKE Dataplane V2, which implements NetworkPolicy via Cilium/eBPF, is built into Google Distributed Cloud bare metal and is always active regardless of this flag.

network_config.island_mode_cidr.pod_addr.description: All pods in the cluster are assigned an RFC1918 IPv4 address from these ranges. This field cannot be changed after creation.
network_config.island_mode_cidr.pod_addr.rationale: The RFC1918 CIDR ranges pods are assigned from are an operational addressing choice for the cluster's internal network plan, outside the scope of a security policy.

network_config.island_mode_cidr.service_.description: All services in the cluster are assigned an RFC1918 IPv4 address from these ranges. This field cannot be changed after creation.
network_config.island_mode_cidr.service_.rationale: Service address CIDR blocks are not important enough to have security implications.

network_config.multiple_network_interfac.description:
When set network_config.advanced_networking is automatically
set to true.
network_config.multiple_network_interfac.rationale: Enables pods to attach multiple network interfaces; an immutable, environment-specific network-topology choice fixed at cluster creation. Neither enabled nor disabled is inherently the safer state - it depends on the customer's own network segmentation design - so it is not a useful policy target.

node_access_config.description: Specifies the node access related settings for the bare metal user cluster.

node_access_config.login_user.description:
LoginUser is the user name used to access node machines.
It defaults to "root" if not set.
node_access_config.login_user.rationale: The OS username used to access node machines (defaults to root). It is an environment-specific operational value; a generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain which login account a team uses, so it is not a useful policy target.

node_config.max_pods_per_node.description:
The maximum number of pods a node can run. The size of the CIDR range
assigned to the node will be derived from this parameter.
node_config.max_pods_per_node.rationale: Controls pod density/resource allocation per node; an operational sizing choice, not an access or exposure control.

proxy.no_proxy.description:
A list of IPs, hostnames, and domains that should skip the proxy.
For example: ["127.0.0.1", "example.com", ".corp", "localhost"].
proxy.no_proxy.rationale: Defines the endpoints excluded from proxy routing; a network configuration choice, not an access-control setting.

proxy.uri.description:
Specifies the address of your proxy server.
For Example: http://domain
WARNING: Do not provide credentials in the format
of http://(username:password@)domain these will be rejected by the server.
proxy.uri.rationale: Points at the customer's own proxy server; an environment-specific infrastructure reference with no universal 'safe' value, the same reasoning already applied to other environment-specific endpoints on this resource.

security_config.description: Specifies the security related settings for the Bare Metal User Cluster.

security_config.authorization.description: Configures user access to the Bare Metal User cluster.

security_config.authorization.admin_user.description: Users that will be granted the cluster-admin role on the cluster, providing full access to the cluster.
The name of the user, e.g. 'my-gcp-id@gmail.com'.
security_config.authorization.admin_user.rationale: Names a single admin principal as an arbitrary identity string (e.g. 'my-gcp-id@gmail.com'), not a collection of IAM principals with a wildcard/public-member risk (unlike a members list that can include 'allUsers'/'allAuthenticatedUsers'). There is no generically 'unsafe' username value to blacklist and no wildcard concept to guard against here, so a platform policy cannot meaningfully police which specific identity a customer names as admin.

storage.lvp_node_mounts_config.description:
Specifies the config for local PersistentVolumes backed
by mounted node disks. These disks need to be formatted and mounted by the
user, which can be done before or after cluster creation.

storage.lvp_node_mounts_config.path.rationale: While mounting a sensitive host root path (e.g. '/', '/etc', '/root', '/boot', '/proc', '/sys', '/var/run/docker.sock') is a documented risk, a platform-level policy here cannot structurally validate host filesystem layouts across disparate node architectures - what counts as a safe or sensitive mount point depends on each deployment's own host provisioning and storage design. This makes it an environment-dependent storage design choice rather than a platform-enforceable control.

storage.lvp_node_mounts_config.storage_c.description: The StorageClass name that PVs will be created with.
storage.lvp_node_mounts_config.storage_c.rationale: A Kubernetes StorageClass name; an identifier/reference, not itself an access-control setting.

storage.lvp_share_config.description:
Specifies the config for local PersistentVolumes backed by
subdirectories in a shared filesystem. These subdirectores are
automatically created during cluster creation.

storage.lvp_share_config.shared_path_pv_.description: The number of subdirectories to create under path.
storage.lvp_share_config.shared_path_pv_.rationale: The number of subdirectories to create under the shared path; numeric capacity sizing, an operational choice with no access-control implication.

storage.lvp_share_config.lvp_config.description: Defines the machine path and storage class for the LVP Share.

storage.lvp_share_config.lvp_config.path.rationale: The host machine filesystem path mounted into the cluster as a local PersistentVolume - functionally a hostPath-style mount. Pointing it at a sensitive system path (e.g. '/', '/etc', '/root', '/boot', '/proc', '/sys', '/var/run/docker.sock') exposes host filesystem content or control-plane sockets to workloads, a well-established Kubernetes container-escape/privilege-escalation vector. Unlike a customer's own IP addressing, dangerous path roots are identifiable in the abstract, so a blacklist of known-sensitive host paths is a meaningful policy target even though the full safe path space is customer-specific.

storage.lvp_share_config.lvp_config.stor.description: The StorageClass name that PVs will be created with.
storage.lvp_share_config.lvp_config.stor.rationale: A Kubernetes StorageClass name; an identifier/reference, not itself an access-control setting.
